brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact: HBM4 pricing power confirmed, CoWoS bottleneck easing, DRAM/NAND contracts +60-75% QoQ in Q2
brief.summary: <cite index="22-5,22-9">Hyperscalers collectively guided $700 billion capex for 2026, nearly double 2025 spend</cite>, with <cite index="29-4">supply constraints rather than demand constraints</cite> driving memory allocation. <cite index="13-2,13-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 while NAND Flash jumped 70-75% QoQ</cite>, following <cite index="19-5">Q1 surges of 90-95% DRAM and 55-60% NAND</cite>. <cite index="6-1,6-6">HBM3E costs ~$300 per 36GB stack as of April 2026, with HBM4 expected at ~$500 per 48GB stack</cite>; <cite index="8-3">Samsung negotiating HBM4 at ~$700 per unit, 20-30% premium over prior gen</cite>. <cite index="35-3,35-5">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026, with monthly capacity reaching 120,000-140,000 wafers</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="42-5">SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 vs Samsung's 35%</cite>, but <cite index="44-5">SK's share reportedly dipped from ~69% to 58% YoY as Samsung ramps</cite>. <cite index="8-6,8-7,8-9">Samsung secured Nvidia's 'Vera Rubin' platform with HBM4, targeting ~30% of Nvidia HBM4 supply vs SK's ~70%</cite>. <cite index="9-11,9-12">SK Hynix wants $600/unit for HBM4 12-stack (30-40% premium over HBM3E) but Nvidia delaying contract, using Samsung as pricing leverage</cite>. <cite index="44-7,44-8">HBM4 involves 50% cost-per-bit increase; SK expects 40% price premium but faces margin pressure from base-die outsourcing</cite>, while <cite index="9-16">Samsung has foundry advantage producing base die in-house</cite>. Near-term relative call: neutral-to-slight-Samsung-tilt on HBM4 share gains and Nvidia qualification momentum offsetting SK's lead time advantage. Watch <cite index="43-1">SK's HBM4E sample timing (June-July 2026 shipments possible)</cite> vs Samsung's HBM4 ramp as next inflection.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-upcycle acceleration with structural tightness through 2027
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-2,10-3">Q1 2026 DRAM contracts +55-60% QoQ, NAND +33-38% QoQ, driven by widening supply-demand gap as CSPs secure capacity</cite>. <cite index="10-4,10-5">DRAM manufacturers reallocating advanced nodes toward server DRAM and HBM, constraining supply to other applications</cite>. <cite index="4-10">ASP gap between HBM3E and DDR5 expected to narrow significantly in 2026</cite> but <cite index="4-12,4-13">HBM investment tightening supply-demand balance for standard DRAM; server DDR5 emerging as second major pillar alongside HBM</cite>. <cite index="10-12,14-6">Enterprise SSDs expected to become largest NAND application in 2026; meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028</cite>. <cite index="11-5,11-6,11-7">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability; memory rally projected past 2028</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-4,1-5">HBM3E demand exceeded expectations following H200 export approval to China (6 stacks per H200); Nvidia planning 40,000-80,000 H200 chips from initial inventory</cite>. <cite index="1-8,1-10">Google TPU (8 HBM3E stacks) and Amazon Trainium3 (4 stacks) shipments begin 2026</cite>; <cite index="1-9">HBM content per accelerator up 20-30% vs prior gen</cite>. <cite index="1-12">Samsung and SK Hynix prioritizing HBM4 ramp keeps HBM3E supply tight, lagging demand</cite>. <cite index="2-1">Goldman expects HBM3E prices to decline 28% YoY in 2026 ($15/GB to $10/GB) under competitive pressure</cite>, but <cite index="1-3,1-4">~20% price hikes for 2026 reported as HBM4 market entry delayed and AI accelerator launches sustain HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="6-11,6-12">B200 with 8 HBM3E stacks costs $2,400 in memory alone, exceeding logic die cost; supply constrained through 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-6,9-7">Nvidia prioritizing lower HBM price over power efficiency; Samsung HBM3E qualification expected ~Aug 15</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: US-Iran ceasefire deal lifts Samsung +6%, SK Hynix +5% in premarket; stocks closed +4.5% and +6.4% on June 15
news_pulse.source: Seoul Economic Daily / Korea Economic Daily
news_pulse.implication: Geopolitical risk premium unwinding; focus shifting from macro to earnings into Q2 results. NXT premarket showing continued momentum June 16 (+2.3% Samsung, +2.8% SK Hynix as of 8:09am).

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; monthly capacity 120k-140k wafers
news_pulse.implication: Packaging bottleneck easing faster than expected. Nvidia's 60-70% CoWoS allocation through 2026 confirmed; incremental capacity benefits AMD, Broadcom ASICs. Positive read-through for HBM attach rates and Samsung/SK Hynix utilization.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix preparing HBM4E samples, shipments possible June-July 2026; Samsung already shipping HBM4
news_pulse.implication: Next-gen HBM race tightening. SK Hynix HBM4E (7th gen) timing vs Samsung's HBM4 volume ramp critical for H2 share dynamics. Nvidia Vera Rubin platform launch timing key catalyst.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $700B (MS $190B, Amazon $200B, Alphabet $185B, Meta $135B); 2027 estimates now >$1T
news_pulse.implication: Structural bid under memory through 2027+. Meta Q1 capex doubled YoY ($13B to $20B); Alphabet $17B to $36B. GPU/CPU depreciation (3-5yr) driving operating margin pressure but ROIC rising, sustaining cycle.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung negotiating HBM4 at ~$700/unit, 20-30% premium over HBM3E; Nvidia Vera Rubin platform confirmed customer
news_pulse.implication: Samsung pricing power recovering after trailing SK Hynix in HBM3E. Foundry integration (base die in-house) vs SK's TSMC outsourcing gives Samsung structural cost advantage in HBM4 despite higher initial costs.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ; Q1 was +90-95% DRAM, +55-60% NAND
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum sustained but decelerating in DRAM (from 90-95% to 58-63%), accelerating in NAND (55-60% to 70-75%). Enterprise SSD demand (AI data centers) outpacing client; cloud LTAs locking supply through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix struck 900k DRAM wafer/month supply deal with OpenAI for Stargate; Samsung P5 fab 2028, SK M15X mid-2027
news_pulse.implication: Stargate project (OpenAI/SoftBank/Oracle $500B) underpinning long-term HBM/DRAM demand visibility. New fab timing (2027-2028) confirms capacity crunch extends through 2026-2027.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman: Samsung HBM3E priced 5% below SK Hynix; Samsung may cut further to regain share; HBM3E $15→$10/GB (-28% YoY)
news_pulse.implication: Confirms Samsung aggressive pricing posture in HBM3E to close gap with SK Hynix and secure Nvidia/hyperscaler qualifications. HBM4 40% premium over HBM3E partially offsets ASP pressure.

brief.derivatives_signal: No derivatives or options data in payload. NXT premarket (June 16, 8:09am KST): Samsung 345.5k (+2.32%), SK Hynix 2.352m (+2.80%). Leverage ETF holders underwater: KODEX Samsung single-stock leverage needs +14.25% underlying move to recover June 2 peak; SK Hynix leverage needs +9.65%. Geopolitical risk premium compression (US-Iran ceasefire) driving short-term momentum but watch for profit-taking into Q2 earnings (late July typical). KOSPI June 15 close: Samsung 337k, SK Hynix 2.288m.
